evidence: Mad Professor is widely described in music journalism as continuing King Tubby's studio-built, desk-as-instrument approach to dub, including building his own mixing board as Tubby did, though he has not, in the sources checked here, named Tubby as a direct personal teacher.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Both men's records treat the mixing desk itself, not a mixed-down finished master, as the instrument being played live. The specific tools differ by a decade of electronics, but the gesture is the same.

explanation: Tubby was an electronics repairman who modified his own desk. A decade later in London, Mad Professor, also trained in electronics, did the same thing and used it the same way. It is held at consensus, not documented, because the likeness is strong and widely noted but there is no specific sourced claim that Tubby taught him. It is stated carefully rather than upgraded, since the two may partly have arrived at the same place separately, from the same limits: cheap secondhand electronics and a willingness to modify them.
